Get started Detection Integrations
Kitty · iTerm2 · Sixel · Half blocks

Images in the terminal. No dependencies.

A .NET library that draws images with the best protocol the terminal has. Detection reads the environment, then asks the terminal once, and never hangs. The core publishes with NativeAOT.

Get started → How detection works
$ dotnet add package Nullean.TerminalImages

Everything between pixels and a terminal

The pieces are plain C#, so there is nothing to install beside the package.

no dependencies
A core with no package references

The PNG codec, the resampler and all four encoders are managed code. No SkiaSharp, no ImageSharp, no native assets: a NativeAOT tcat is 1.7 MB.
detection
One question, and an answer that ends the wait

The probe ends with a request every terminal answers. A silent terminal costs 250 ms; a talkative one costs a round trip.
four encoders
Kitty, iTerm2, Sixel, half blocks

Median-cut Sixel with dithering, Kitty chunks with optional compression, and half blocks in 24-bit or 256 colours.
overrides
An override for every guess

NULLEAN_TERMINAL_IMAGES forces a protocol, and the result lists a line of reasons for every decision it made.
integrations
In your framework

A renderable for Spectre.Console, a view for Terminal.Gui v2, and WriteImage for XenoAtom.Terminal.
tmux and ssh
Passthrough built in

Images are wrapped for tmux, one sequence at a time, and the probe is sent through to the outer terminal.

Detect, then draw

The renderer scales the image to fit, picks the encoder, and leaves the cursor below the image.

● ● ●Program.cs
var capabilities = await TerminalImageDetector.DetectAsync();
var renderer = new TerminalImageRenderer(capabilities);
renderer.RenderPng(File.ReadAllBytes("photo.png"), Console.Out);

Asking the terminal, once

Terminals answer in order, and every one of them answers Device Attributes. So that goes last.

● ● ●the probe, in one write
ESC _ G i=31,s=1,v=1,a=q,t=d,f=24;AAAA ESC \  Kitty query
ESC [ > 0 q                                       name and version
ESC [ 16 t                                        cell size in pixels
ESC [ c                                           the sentinel: DA1

Cheapest evidence first

Detection stops as soon as it has an answer it can trust.

  1. OverrideThe NULLEAN_TERMINAL_IMAGES variable, or code. Never probed.
  2. GatesOutput redirected, or TERM=dumb: nothing is drawn.
  3. EnvironmentKitty, Ghostty, iTerm2, WezTerm, Windows Terminal and others, with no I/O.
  4. ProbeOne write to /dev/tty, with a timeout that applies only when the terminal says nothing.

And it says why

The result lists what was found and a line for every decision. This is a scripted terminal that answers like WezTerm.

Four ways to draw

The renderer picks, in the order your terminal prefers.

ProtocolSent asScalingTerminals
Kittyraw RGBA in 4096-byte base64 chunks, or a PNGby the terminalKitty, Ghostty
iTerm2a PNG file in one OSC 1337 sequenceby the terminaliTerm2, WezTerm, Konsole, mintty
Sixel6-pixel bands with a palette, run-length encodednone: drawn at pixel sizefoot, Windows Terminal, xterm, WezTerm
Half blocks▀ with a foreground and a background colournoneanything with colour

In your framework

Each host is its own package. The core never references one.

Nullean.TerminalImages.Spectre
Spectre.Console

A TerminalImage renderable. Half blocks use Spectre's own colours, so they downgrade with the console.
Nullean.TerminalImages.TerminalGui
Terminal.Gui v2

A TerminalImageView that feeds Terminal.Gui's raster pipeline, and detection that sees through tmux and SSH.
Nullean.TerminalImages.XenoAtom
XenoAtom.Terminal

terminal.WriteImage(image), written atomically, with no SkiaSharp.

What is verified

Verified: the encoders, PNG codec, resampler, detection logic and renderer, with unit tests that were checked by breaking the code on purpose; the terminal probe, by running the published NativeAOT binary in a pseudo-terminal with a scripted terminal, on macOS and Linux; the Terminal.Gui view in a live Terminal.Gui application; XenoAtom on its in-memory backend.

Not yet verified: output on real terminals (Kitty, Ghostty, iTerm2, WezTerm, foot, Windows Terminal, xterm), and tmux or SSH. The terminal-specific choices come from how other tools and the terminals' own documentation treat them. If one is wrong, tcat --diagnostics shows why, and an override fixes it.
